```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(cytoJointR)
# Optional packages: chunks that need them run only when they are installed.
has_pkg <- function(p) nzchar(system.file(package = p)) && requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
has_compass <- has_pkg("COMPASS")
has_polyics <- has_pkg("polyICSFlow")
```

This vignette goes from one row per event to gated patterns, COMPASS and
polyICSFlow scores, and the fluorescence-aware scores of cytoJointR. It uses
simulated cells, so the true gate is known (fluorescence 0).
Optional packages (COMPASS: `r if (has_compass) "installed" else "not installed, its chunk is shown but not run"`;
polyICSFlow: `r if (has_polyics) "installed" else "not installed, its chunk is shown but not run"`)
are checked at run time.

## Cells and samples

`cells` has one row per event: `sample_id` and one fluorescence column per
marker. Events must already be inside the parent population (for example live
CD4 T cells). `samples` has one row per sample with `donor_id`, `visit` (a factor
with explicit levels), `parent_population` and `condition`.

```{r data}
sim <- cj_simulate_cells(donors = 10, cells_per_sample = 1500, seed = 1)
cells <- sim$cells
markers <- c("IFNG", "TNF", "IL2")
samples <- unique(cells[c("sample_id", "donor_id", "condition")])
samples$visit <- factor("v1")
samples$parent_population <- "CD4"
head(cells[c("sample_id", markers)], 3)
table(samples$condition)
```

### Cells from FCS files or a GatingSet

Two readers build `cells` from cytometry files. `cj_read_fcs()` reads one FCS
file per sample, applies the file's own spillover matrix and keeps the chosen
markers, by channel name or exact channel description. The files must hold the
parent population only, for example CD4 T cells exported from FlowJo.
`cj_cells_from_gatingset()` takes the events of one gated population of a
flowWorkspace `GatingSet`, for data gated in FlowJo (imported with CytoML) or
with an openCyto template. Neither reader transforms; choose the transform in
`cj_gate()`, and use `transform = "none"` for GatingSet data that are already
transformed.

```{r read, eval = FALSE}
files <- list.files("exports/CD4", pattern = "\\.fcs$", full.names = TRUE)
cells <- cj_read_fcs(files, c(IFNG = "IFNg BV421", TNF = "TNFa PE", IL2 = "IL2 APC"))
cells <- cj_cells_from_gatingset(gs, "CD4", c(IFNG = "IFNg BV421", TNF = "TNFa PE", IL2 = "IL2 APC"))
```

The simulator calls the unstimulated sample `"unstim"`. The package wants
`"control"` internally, so every function takes `control = "unstim"` and
recodes it.

## Gate

`cj_gate()` finds one threshold per marker on all control events pooled over
donors. The transform must be stated: `"none"` means these cells are already on
the analysis scale. For raw fluorescence use `transform = "asinh"` with a
`cofactor`, or pass a function.

```{r gate}
gate <- cj_gate(cells, markers, samples, transform = "none", control = "unstim")
gate
```

The default `"tail"` method runs in base R. It takes the main peak of the
pooled control density as the negative population and puts the cut 3.09 spreads
above it. `method = "quantile"` takes a control quantile. `method = "mindensity"`
calls `openCyto::gate_mindensity()` when openCyto is installed (otherwise it
warns and uses the quantile). `thresholds = c(IFNG = 0.3, ...)` sets them by hand.
Always look at the gate.

```{r gate-plot}
cj_plot_gate(gate)
```

Here the true gate is 0. The tail gate misclassifies
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(unlist(lapply(markers, function(m) (cells[[m]] > gate$thresholds[[m]]) != (cells[[m]] > 0)))))`
of cells against it.

### When the control is not a clean Gaussian peak

The tail gate reads the negative peak from its lower half. It fails when the
upper tail is heavy or when batches shift the channel offset. Three options
address that, and each reads control events only.

`method = "auto"` picks tail or quantile per marker. Its statistic is the *tail
ratio*: the distance from the mode to the 99th percentile of the control events,
over what the lower-half spread predicts for a symmetric peak. It is about 1 for
a clean peak. Above 1.5 (the 99th percentile of the Gaussian null at 1000 events
or more) the marker gets the control quantile, unless over 3% of the control lies
above the tail cut. Then it is more likely a positive population than a tail, and
the tail cut stays. The reason is in `gate$auto`.

```{r gate-auto}
sg <- cj_simulate_gate_cells(c("clean", "skewed"), c("IFNG", "IL21"), batches = 3,
                             batch_shift = 1.5, samples_per_batch = 3,
                             cells_per_sample = 2000, seed = 2)
g_auto <- cj_gate(sg$cells, c("IFNG", "IL21"), sg$samples, method = "auto",
                  transform = "none", control = "unstim", by = "batch")
g_auto$auto[c("marker", "tail_ratio", "excess", "choice", "reason")]
```

`by = "batch"` finds one cut per batch (here a column of the sample table) and
`cj_from_cells()` applies it. A batch with fewer than `min_batch_events` control
events warns and takes the pooled cut. Three QC flags are printed and drawn on the
gate plot:

* `cut_in_broad_tail`: the control density at the cut is above 5% of the peak.
* `high_control_positive`: over 1% of the control lies above the tail-rule cut.
* `batch_cut_spread`: the batch cuts span more than one negative-peak spread.

```{r gate-qc}
g_auto
cj_plot_gate(g_auto)
```

A flag is a prompt to look, not a verdict. A marker with real unstimulated
expression (IL-10-like) is flagged `high_control_positive`, and no automatic cut
is reliable there; set it by hand or gate on the stimulated-minus-control contrast.

For raw fluorescence, `cofactor = "auto"` (or `cj_cofactor()`) sets the asinh
cofactor to 3 times the one-sided spread of the negative peak of the raw control
events, per marker. The negative peak and the cut then sit in the near-linear zone
of the transform. The rule is scale-free: rescaling a channel rescales its cofactor.

```{r cofactor}
raw <- sg$cells
raw[c("IFNG", "IL21")] <- 400 * raw[c("IFNG", "IL21")]  # arbitrary raw units
cj_cofactor(raw, c("IFNG", "IL21"), sg$samples, control = "unstim")
```

**Evidence.** The rule and its constants were fixed on simulated controls with a
known truth (`scripts/97_*`, `98_*`, `99_*`, `101_*` in the reproducibility
repository, run directory `runs/2026-11-08_gating-hardening/`), and then compared
with expert FlowJo gates on two public datasets, once.

| Held-out FlowJo comparison (Cohen's kappa, stimulated positive control, mean of 9 markers) | mean kappa |
|---|---|
| old: tail, pooled cut, fixed cofactor (2000 malaria, 150 C9orf72) | 0.604 |
| tail, pooled, `cofactor = "auto"` | 0.791 |
| tail, `by = "screen"`, fixed cofactor | 0.637 |
| tail, `by = "screen"`, `cofactor = "auto"` | 0.825 |
| `method = "auto"`, pooled, fixed cofactor | 0.599 |
| `method = "auto"`, `by`, `cofactor = "auto"` | 0.761 |

Malaria has no batch column, so `by` changes only the four C9orf72 markers. The
comparison was run once on the frozen code (commit bbb996e) and no rule was
changed afterwards. The gain comes from the cofactor rule (malaria IL-21 kappa
0.33 to 0.72, CD107a 0.75 to 0.91; C9orf72 IL-17 0.36 to 0.94) and from batch
cuts (C9orf72 IL-4 0.74 to 0.85, IL-10 0.09 to 0.23 to
0.64). The tail/quantile selector did not help: it switched only C9orf72 IFN-gamma
(pooled, fixed cofactor) and IL-10 (with the auto cofactor), and both lost
agreement (0.97 to 0.92, 0.37 to 0.06). The IL-21 failure was a transform failure,
not a heavy tail: its tail ratio is 0.4. So `method = "auto"` stays experimental,
and the recommended call is `method = "tail"` (default) with `by` and
`cofactor = "auto"`. The QC flags describe the control distribution; they did not
track FlowJo agreement one for one (they fire on C9orf72 IFN-gamma, kappa 0.97,
because of screen offsets, and stay silent on IL-21). The cofactor and batch gains
were each frozen as components before the comparison, but the recommended
combination was picked among eight scored candidates, so its kappa is optimistic.


## Cells to `cj_data`

`cj_from_cells()` applies the gate, tabulates exact patterns per sample and
returns the same `cj_data` the count workflow uses, so `cj_describe()`,
`cj_fit()` and `cj_scores()` work on it. It also keeps the per-pattern sums of
`X - t` and `(X - t)^2` that the fluorescence scores need.

```{r data-object}
x <- cj_from_cells(cells, samples = samples, gate = gate)
x
dim(x$intensity$sx)  # sample x pattern x marker
```

## Fluorescence-aware scores

`cj_fluorescence_scores()` returns one row per donor, stimulation, visit and
marker. All scores are descriptive: plug-in estimates from the events, in
transformed fluorescence units per parent cell. Donors without a control are
listed and omitted.

```{r fluor}
fs <- cj_fluorescence_scores(x, n_boot = 100, seed = 1)
head(fs[c("donor_id", "marker", "nicr", "nicr_lo", "nicr_hi", "poly_nicr", "iw_pfs")], 6)
```

* `nicr`: net integrated cytokine response of the marker, stimulated minus
  control burden. Markers are never summed.
* `poly_nicr`: the same over patterns with two or more positive markers.
* `nicr_freq`, `nicr_int`, `nicr_unmatched`: an exact split of `nicr` into a
  change in how many cells are in each pattern and a change in how bright they
  are. They add up to `nicr`:

```{r decomp}
with(fs, max(abs(nicr - nicr_freq - nicr_int - nicr_unmatched)))
```

* `fis`: intensity shift under fixed reference weights, `NA` with a reason where
  a reference pattern has no cells. Controls hold few polyfunctional cells, so
  use `reference = "single"` to ask for the shift among cells positive for that
  marker alone.
* `iw_fs`, `iw_pfs` (experimental): COMPASS's FS and PFS weights applied to the
  net burden of each marker in each subset instead of a response probability.

```{r fis}
fs1 <- cj_fluorescence_scores(x, reference = "single")
table(fis_available = !is.na(fs1$fis))
```

The bootstrap resamples events within each sample. Its intervals cover cell
sampling only. Donors are the replicates, so compare groups across donors.

```{r nicr-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
d <- fs[fs$marker == "IFNG", ]
d$donor_id <- factor(d$donor_id, levels = d$donor_id[order(d$nicr)])
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(.data$nicr, .data$donor_id)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(xmin = .data$nicr_lo, xmax = .data$nicr_hi)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "NICR of IFNG (transformed units per parent cell), 95% cell bootstrap",
                y = NULL)
```

## COMPASS and polyICSFlow

`cj_run_compass()` wraps `cj_compass()` and returns a tidy FS, PFS and response
table per donor. The full `cj_compass` object is in `attr(, "compass")`.

```{r compass, eval = has_compass}
cp <- cj_run_compass(x, iterations = 200, replications = 2, seed = 1)
head(cp[c("donor_id", "compass_FS", "compass_PFS")], 4)
```

A stimulated sample without a control is dropped by default. Set
`missing_control = "donor"` to borrow the same donor's control from the nearest
other visit, or `"population"` to compare the sample with the other donors'
controls (COMPASS integrates out each donor's control proportions, so a zero
control row contributes nothing). The `control_source` column says which rows
were not paired. A borrowed control assumes the background does not change
between visits, and the population control assumes this donor's background is
like the others'; see `docs/adr/0003-compass-missing-control.md` for the
simulation behind these cautions.

| Option | Setting | FPR, non-paired | FPR, paired |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"population"` | moderate effect | 0.19 to 0.39 | 0.05 to 0.10 |
| `"population"` | rare, weak effect | 0.01 to 0.03, TPR 0.20 to 0.70 (paired 0.64) | 0.01 |
| `"donor"` | stable background | 0.06 to 0.17 | 0.05 to 0.08 |
| `"donor"` | background x1.5 at visit 2 | 0.4 to 0.55 pooled (0.81 to 0.94 later visit) | 0.06 to 0.19 |

Both options are experimental and best used to rank donors. `"donor"` checks the
donor's other controls first and sets `control_shift_check` to `ok`, `differs`
or `untestable`; the last two warn. Details: ADR 0003.

```{r compass-missing, eval = FALSE}
cj_run_compass(x, missing_control = "donor", iterations = 200, replications = 2)
```

`cj_run_polyicsflow()` runs polyICSFlow's marker-combination and
background-subtraction functions on the same counts. polyICSFlow clips each
pattern at zero, so `polyics_net_any` is not the signed net percent of
`cj_describe()`.

```{r polyics, eval = has_polyics}
pf <- cj_run_polyicsflow(x)
head(pf$net)
```

## Magnitudes beside COMPASS calls

COMPASS says who responds, not how large the response is. `cj_compass_report()`
puts the cytoJointR magnitude and a 90% interval beside each COMPASS call, one
row per donor, stimulation and visit. The default magnitude is C0-EB, an
empirical-Bayes pooled conjugate model: it needs no Stan and runs in seconds.
`magnitude_model = "c0"` is the plain independent-Dirichlet version. `magnitude_model = "m1dm"` uses the structured posterior of
[cj_fit()] instead. From a cell data frame the report also carries NICR and
Poly-NICR with a cell bootstrap, per marker, in `attr(, "markers")`.

```{r report, eval = has_compass}
rep <- cj_compass_report(cells, markers, samples, transform = "none", control = "unstim",
                         gate_args = list(method = "quantile"), n_boot = 50,
                         compass_args = list(iterations = 200, replications = 2))
rep
rep[c("donor_id", "compass_response_degree1", "rms", "rms_lower", "rms_upper", "concordance")]
head(attr(rep, "markers")[c("contrast_id", "marker", "nicr", "nicr_lo", "nicr_hi")], 4)
```

`concordance` compares the two answers. The COMPASS call is a response
probability above 0.5. The magnitude is positive when the lower end of the RMS
interval is above 0. `response_without_magnitude` (COMPASS calls a response, the
RMS interval includes 0) and `magnitude_without_response` mark rows to look at.
They are prompts, not errors: a call and an interval answer different questions.
In simulation (`?cj_compass_report` has the numbers), C0-EB and `m1dm` rank donor
RMS better than COMPASS FS within a data set, also at a rare, weak response,
where plain C0 does not. The intervals describe the sampled donor-visit only,
and CPS from C0 or C0-EB should not be used (take it from `m1dm`).

```{r report-plot, eval = has_compass, fig.height = 3.5}
cj_plot_compass_report(rep)
```

Position is the RMS with its interval; colour is the COMPASS response
probability; triangles are discordant rows.

## Everything at once

`cj_quickstart()` chains gate, data, description, fluorescence scores and, when
installed, COMPASS and polyICSFlow. Add `fit = TRUE` (and `epsilon`) to fit the
count model and get the cytoJointR scores; that needs CmdStan.

```{r quickstart}
qs <- cj_quickstart(cells, markers, samples, transform = "none", control = "unstim",
                    run = character())
names(qs)
```
